npr_news.source: Talkers estimate via Wikipedia (List of most-listened-to radio programs)
npr_news.quote: All Things Considered | News broadcast | NPR | p.m. drive | 14.7
npr_news.notes: Talkers Magazine estimate reproduced in Wikipedia's table 'the 20 most-listened-to radio shows in the United States according to weekly cumulative listenership'. Talkers calls its own figures non-scientific and the table is undated, so this is a secondary estimate, not a measured audience. Radio has no public per-host Nielsen table: Arbitron/Nielsen do not compile nationwide by host and Talkers' own top-talk-audiences page is now 404. Outlet is NPR's news magazines; All Things Considered (14.7m) is the larger, Morning Edition is 13.1m in the same table, and the two audiences overlap. NPR itself states a 42m weekly cross-platform audience (nationalpublicmedia.com/audience), a broader measure not comparable with the per-programme figures used here.
